key_idea: Trips form a DAG (i before j if a driver can finish i and reach j's start in time), and the minimum number of drivers is a minimum path cover = k - maximum bipartite matching.
sketch: Floyd-Warshall on the 100-node directed graph gives all travel times. Add edge i->j when t_i + d(u_i,v_i) + d(v_i,u_j) <= t_j; since every trip takes positive time the relation is acyclic and transitive, so minimum vertex-disjoint path cover equals minimum chain cover. Run Hopcroft-Karp on the split graph with up to 10^6 edges and print k - matching. Complexity O(n^3 + k^2 sqrt k). Pitfalls: roads are one-directional, trips ending after minute 480 are fine, and equal times allow chaining (<=).
